answer: One identity claims a ledge juniper windbreak row above one orchard block, with an 80-credit bond. Each epoch it files juniper stem count, length, gaps, and ledge key. An orchard auditor measures both sides and recomputes shelter from the public windbreak table; a short row, gap, or reused key burns it. First filing: 33 credits, k-th: 33+6(k-1); the 1,000th costs 6,027, and 1,000 fakes pay 3,030,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-windbreak ring fails because one row shelters only its own block and paired readings expose sharing. An honest grower pays 33 once and recovers it after a clean epoch.
